correctness.rationale: For k=n*pi+z/(n*pi), y=k²sin²k tends to z². Independently checked the source-derived fifth-root cubic: at even parity j=0 it factors y²(y-8), and j=1..4 as omega*y(y-5)(y-8); odd parity factors (y-4)(y-(6-2sqrt(5)))(y-(6+2sqrt(5))) at j=0 and (y-1)(y-4)(y-(6 +/- 2sqrt(5))) at j=1..4. Positive y roots are distinct, hence nonzero z zeros simple and persist under uniform secular asymptotics. This proves exactly the stated nonzero scaled branches but not branches with z->0, multiplicities or higher order.
